method: One individually attributed external public-web search per hypothetical seller case, followed by feedback-generated buyer-job searches for zero-observation cases and one representative per sector. At most the first five parsed search sources per query were retained. Captured excerpts were assessed through PULL source policy and observation logic; this is not a live production-provider or end-to-end buyer-finding evaluation.
limitations: Search results can be irrelevant, stale, seller advertisements, job listings or incomplete.
Request publication dates were not established by this pass.
Policy admissibility, lexical acceptance and recovered observations are not independent relevance, buyer-finding or private-ownership verification.
Case products, seller situations, buyer jobs and triggers remain hypothetical.
No outreach, buyer response or transaction was executed.
Adaptive selection is nonrandom and cannot establish a causal performance improvement.
Only the queries in the recorded first and adaptive passes were executed; other suggestions remain unexecuted.
